thing.x: Opened in US cinemas on 25 June 1982, two weeks after E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, and was a box-office disappointment.
Adapted from John W. Campbell Jr.'s 1938 novella Who Goes There?, which had already inspired the 1951 film The Thing from Another World.
Rob Bottin, then in his early twenties, designed most of the creature effects. Stan Winston's team built the dog creature.
Ennio Morricone composed the score, a rare case of Carpenter handing a film's music to another composer.
Critics were cold in 1982. Its reputation grew on home video and cable, and it is now ranked among the best horror films of the decade.
